draft.answer: No call contains profanity, insults or hostility, but many contain mild rudeness, mostly curtness, sarcasm and interruptions. The clearest cases are Fable Media (vendor rep condescension and interruption) [C1], Trafford Dental (customer rebukes and vendor talking over her) [C2], and Verity Payments and Pinewood (sharp vendor/customer exchanges) [C3]. Curtness or sarcasm also appears in the other prospect, renewal and cold-call calls [C4], and Greenline and Kestrel were essentially cordial [C5].

claims.text: Fable Media: vendor AE Alastair McCrae interrupted COO Imogen Price ("Yep. Yep. Classic. So that's exactly what we —"), called Zapier "a toy", addressed a prospect as "mate, what's a lost client worth?" (patronising, inferred) and brushed past Ben Foster's objection. Imogen replied curtly ("if you let me finish", "That's not really what I asked.", "We're an agency, Alastair. Nobody's auditing our onboarding process."). Alastair apologised and did not retaliate.

Trafford Dental Group (cold call): Yvonne Deeks was blunt with Alastair McCrae ("You don't actually know anything about us, do you.", "I know what it isn't...", "Look, I'm not trying to be unkind. But you've been talking for three minutes...", "He fixes printers.", "...good luck."). Alastair cut her off ("Exactly. And that's exactly the problem we solve.") and brushed aside her objection. He did not retaliate and later apologised.

Churn and at-risk calls had sharp exchanges. Verity Payments: Sarah Lindqvist called Ruth Adeyemi's answer "accurate and completely useless" (then said she was not attacking her), Ruth replied "Then we don't say it, do we." and told Kwame Boateng his account was "below median" (blunt, arguably condescending, inferred), and Kwame was curt ("You asked.", "You weren't there in February."). Oakhill Property: Hazel Wren refused curtly ("Alastair, no. I'm not doing that.") and was sarcastic ("At least you're honest."); Ruth said she was on the call "because it's a churn". Pinewood Insurance: Ruth's "bus factor of one and the bus arrived" could land as insensitive, Leo Grant's "customer in May than a lawsuit in March" read as a veiled threat (inferred), and Graham Attwood was curt and sarcastic ("Five. Thank you, Nadia.").

Other calls had mild curtness, sarcasm or interruptions, mostly from customers and largely inferred as non-hostile. Acme Logistics: Rachel Morgan said "Three. Great." and Tom Alvarez said "We can see your inbox." Cedar & Finch: Sophie Reed said "Can we not?" and "Stop there." BrightPath: Elliot Greene was curt ("It's zero, Priya."). DeltaWorks: Anika Bose was terse ("Everyone says that."). Ember Financial: Noah Williams challenged Hannah Cole in front of the vendor, and Hannah said "Don't flatter me". Harbor Legal: Samir Khan interrupted ("I know.") and Eleanor Brooks said "How reassuring." Inkwell: Olivia Grant and Darren Wu bickered ("Here we go."), and Maya Chen's retort to Darren was curt. Juniper: Marcus Chen was dismissive ("Here we go.", "I appreciate being managed."). Lumen: Fiona Bright and Devan Shah were sarcastic ("Of course there is.", "I'm sure you will."). Halberd: Grace Okonkwo was dismissive ("Seven percent... not worth an hour of my life."). Silverline: Chloe Barnes ("Don't waste them."), Martine Duval ("She said three.") and Leo's "ninety seconds left" were curt. Quarry Ridge: Dermot Kelly said "Well, then you know."
Greenline Energy Services was assessed as having no rude speech beyond mild, laughed-off teasing, and Kestrel Robotics was described as cordial with only light friction.
